cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Steer the Suspicion
cards.instruction: Hide your responsibility by redirecting every new clue toward a safer explanation before anyone can connect it back to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll write to the manufacturer. Your shelf fell because they supplied the wrong bracket.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You fitted it upside down. Look at the arrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll complain about the arrow. I'll hold the bracket while you photograph it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You drew that arrow. I watched you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Photograph both sides, then. I'll put in the complaint that they made us draw our own safety markings.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs manufacturer contact; A3 holds the actual bracket to keep B documenting while changing blame to its arrow; A5 makes A own drawing another manufacturer omission.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 explicitly names the bracket as the held object, removing the arrow/it ambiguity; B4 witnessed drawing remains the inconvenient fact A reframes.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains upside-down fitting and B4 identifies A as the marking author rather than accepting the complaint.

heightening.evidence: B4 authorship causes A5 both-side photos and the safety-markings excuse.

specificity.evidence: A1 shelf and bracket plus A3 named physical object make the shared documentation task legible.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 photo scope and complaint wording are the concrete response to B4; no additional narrative action is needed.
